From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Ben / Dev — see draft answers below (legal-reviewed). I’ve attached an excerpt from the DPA that covers controller/processor and breach obligations (Redwood_DPA_Excerpt-controller-processor.txt) and included the subprocessors CSV.

1) Controller/Processor
- Redwood acts as a Processor with respect to customer-provided data. Zenith Health is the Controller.
- Proposed clause wording (copy/paste into reply to client): "The parties agree that Customer determines the purposes and means of processing Personal Data and is therefore the Controller; Redwood Inference is a Processor acting on Customer's documented instructions, as set forth in the DPA."

2) Subprocessors
- Current subprocessors are listed in subprocessors_list_2026-10.csv (included). Redwood provides notice of new subprocessors by email and via a live list; standard practice is to notify customers at least 15 days prior to onboarding. If Zenith requires 30 days, propose we offer 30 days for any subprocessor that will access production customer data (we can accept that in most cases).

3) Breach notice
- Redwood’s standard is to notify Customers without undue delay and provide an initial notification within 72 hours of confirming a material security incident affecting Customer Data.
- Proposed contact: security-alerts@redwood.ai (primary) and legal@redwood.ai (cc).

4) Data residency & retention
- Technical: we can pin production workspaces to US regions (us-east-1 or us-west-2) for data residency. We maintain clear isolation per workspace and can confirm region by workspace ID.
- Retention: configurable retention windows (30/90/365 days) for logs and temporary KV caches; model outputs and user data can be scheduled for deletion.
- Deletion: we provide APIs for deletion and can issue a signed confirmation of deletion upon request (process typically 7 business days).

5) Logging & Audit
- We retain system access logs and API request logs. Default retention is 90 days; extended retention is available as an add-on. Audit logs include requester IP, timestamp, request id, and action. Role-based access controls and SOC2 controls around log access are in place.

Action: If these answers look good I can draft a short reply to Zenith and include the suggested DPA language + attachments. If they want DPA redlines we can accept 30-day notice for subprocessors and the 72-hour breach notification as contract language.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Excerpt-controller-processor.txt, subprocessors_list_2026-10.csv

- Controller/Processor: Redwood will be Processor; Zenith Health is Controller. Suggested contract text attached (excerpt).
- Subprocessors: current list attached (subprocessors_list_2026-10.csv). Redwood will notify customers of new subprocessors; for production data we can commit to a 30-day notice period.
- Breach notice: Redwood will provide initial notification within 72 hours of confirming a material incident affecting your data. Primary contact: security-alerts@redwood.ai (legal@redwood.ai cc).

- Deletion/certificates: Redwood provides deletion APIs and can issue a signed certificate of deletion within 7 business days of request.
- Logging/audit: default audit/log retention is 90 days; extended retention is available as an add-on. Logs include requester IP, timestamp, request id, and action; RBAC and SOC2 controls govern access.
